correctness.rationale: The fixed-point equation is bijectively equivalent to F(r)=0 with endpoint signs and derivative 2/r+4uηr³sinθ/(1+r²)². At every nonpositive-slope root the critical strength is at least the minimum of (1+t)²/sqrt(4u²−(1+u²−t)²). Exact derivative gives a unique feasible positive quadratic root and the radical E(u). Below E all roots cross upward, so uniqueness; above E phase tuning creates an interior negative-crossing root, forcing at least two additional roots. Sign boundaries and eta<0 symmetry checked. SymPy reproduces the optimizing quadratic and independent numerical witnesses find 3 roots.

value.rationale: A phase-dependent optical ring cavity may have one or multiple steady states; exact onset of achievable multiplicity across all phase detunings is a natural global dynamical boundary. The theorem proves both the all-phase uniqueness region and a constructive three-fixed-point phase above a unique exact radical threshold for every damping u∈(0,1). It is not just an algebraic substitution or one numerical case and separates uniqueness sharply from the more conservative Euclidean contraction criterion.
